[1/2] Make the selected-work heading independent of the number of live public repositories

impact_assessment.why: The live atlas hides a featured card when its repository is no longer public; the heading still said 'Four systems', which would become false.
impact_assessment.benefits: The featured section stays correct whether four, three or more systems are public.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: text-only change; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; policy: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Update the heading and re-run the content tests and live checks.

checkpoints.description: Task 'site-v16' completed successfully.
[1/6] Build searchable atlas metadata, local project pages, verifier conveniences, trust pages, an offline shell, and structured data on top of the live GitHub sync

impact_assessment.why: The atlas now fetches live GitHub data but only exposes five curated filters; repository cards omit language, license and freshness; every card leaves the site immediately; the verifier lacks ID lookup, drag-and-drop and export; there are no security, privacy or accessibility pages; the manifest has no service worker; and the 404 page and structured data are thin.
impact_assessment.benefits: Visitors can search and deep-link projects by text, topic, discipline and recency, open a local project summary with license and README context, verify a certificate from an ID, drop a file, and export the result, read the trust pages, install an offline-capable shell, and reach projects from the 404 page.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds project.html, security/privacy/accessibility pages, security.txt, atlas-snapshot.json and sw.js, no existing URL changes; dependency: no package, browser APIs only; concurrency: one service-worker cache version and one in-flight atlas fetch; state: URL query parameters, session cache and Cache Storage, no credentials; security: untrusted GitHub text stays text, README excerpts are plain text, the service worker caches only GET shell/API responses, and CSP hashes must be regenerated for every inline block
impact_assessment.mitigation: Split into six milestones, pin each with Python and Node tests, mock the GitHub API in Playwright, regenerate CSP hashes, run axe on every new page, and verify the deployed pages against the real API.

[3/6] Local project dossier: project.html, project-core.js and project.js resolve a repository from atlas-snapshot.json or the public API and render metadata plus a plain-text README excerpt; 32 project-page assertions and 78 Python tests pass; checklists: passed

[5/6] Security, privacy and accessibility pages published with .well-known/security.txt, sitemap entries, footer links and README pointers; 78 Python tests and all four suites pass; checklists: passed

Task 'site-v17' completed successfully.
[1/2] Collapse the portfolio header and filter chrome: one-line intro, one search/sort row, count-free discipline chips, no topic chip row, single result count, count-free atlas status

impact_assessment.why: The portfolio stacked five control rows and repeated the repository total four times, burying the cards
impact_assessment.benefits: Cards start sooner; one count per surface; less DOM, CSS and JS to maintain
impact_assessment.risks: contract: chip badges, topic row and count-bearing status text removed; dependency: none; concurrency: one service-worker cache version bump; state: topic deep links and the topic URL parameter still work
impact_assessment.mitigation: Update the Python and Node tests with the markup, keep topic filtering by URL and search, bump the service-worker version, and run every gate

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Portfolio trimmed: one-line intro, search/sort row, six count-free discipline chips, no topic row, one result count, count-free atlas status, service worker v2; ADR-026; 78 Python tests, 52 atlas, 58 verifier and 32 project assertions, 4/4 gates pass; checklists: passed
Task 'portfolio-trim' completed successfully.

[1/4] Put topic chips back inside the discipline row (count-free), add a dossier logo slot and a screenshot gallery fed by a per-repository media manifest that records the commit and date of every capture

impact_assessment.why: The single discipline row lost topic discovery, and dossiers have no logo or screenshot surface even though captures will soon exist
impact_assessment.benefits: One chip row covers discipline and topics; dossiers can show a real logo and commit-stamped screenshots without a build step
impact_assessment.risks: contract: docs/media/<Repo>.json schema and dossier markup; dependency: browser fetch only; concurrency: none; state: media manifests and images, no credentials
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure normalization helpers with Node tests, safe relative media paths only, hidden sections until media exists, Python and Node parity tests
